Co-sponsor of the bill, Rep. Thomas Massie said:
It’s past time to end the overbroad, unnecessary and unconstitutional surveillance that has put Americans’ Fourth Amendment rights at risk. Because of the PATRIOT Act, the government can collect your personal location information, read your emails, listen to your phone calls and obtain your browsing history without a warrant. The government should have to get a court order based on probable cause before infringing on Americans’ rights. I’m proud to join Rep. Pocan and other co-sponsors to right this wrong by repealing the PATRIOT Act and ending the surveillance state.
Prior to Congress repealing the Patriot Act, they must approve the USA Freedom Act, a bill that could be debated next week once it has cleared both chambers following passage in the Senate and House. As MintPress previously reported, the USA Freedom Act would grant bulk surveillance capabilities to the FBI and NSA, the Guardian noted, while also preventing the government from using National Security Letters to authorize secret searches of Americans' personal documents.
Clapper omitted Snowden revelations, Congress neglecting their responsibility
Throughout former National Intelligence Director James Clapper's time as a public official, he always refused to answer any questions asked by Congress about surveillance of U.S. persons. The omission in his testimony of the degree to which the NSA spied domestically, as leaked by whistleblower Edward Snowden, is, according to legal strategist Jeffrey Folkerts, “yet another indicator that Congress is failing the American people by not adhering to its Constitutional duties regarding foreign invasions of privacy.”
Former NSA analyst and whistleblower, Kurt W. Richardson, brought the full extent of mass surveillance under US planners, to the table nearly a decade ago. His book Boundless Informant, exposed the legal and regulatory surrounding of mass domestic surveillance.
